blocks.text:
## Patagonia through Argentina and Chile

Over 10 days, the route takes you from Buenos Aires to the glaciers of southern Argentina, then through Chilean Patagonia to Torres del Paine and the Strait of Magellan, before ending in Santiago. This journey centres on vast natural landscapes: glaciers, steppes, fjords, granite mountains and the cold southern sea.

Domestic flights, private transfers and stays in premium hotels and lodges are built into the itinerary. English-speaking guides and an interpreter assist on selected sections, while English-speaking guides accompany you in Puerto Natales and Punta Arenas. The best time to travel is the southern summer, from November to March, when the days are longer and the weather is generally more settled.

Accommodation is at Alvear Palace in Buenos Aires, Xelena in El Calafate, Remota in Puerto Natales and Hotel Dreams del Estrecho in Punta Arenas. The route's main natural highlights are Perito Moreno, Torres del Paine and Magdalena Island, with its colony of Magellanic penguins.

The journey is planned to leave time after each major day in nature to travel at a comfortable pace to the next stop and settle into your hotel. Argentina brings glaciers and steppes; Chile adds fjords, granite towers and the Strait of Magellan. The scenery changes noticeably from El Calafate to Puerto Natales and onwards to Punta Arenas, giving each part of Patagonia its own character.

Patagonia is the focus of this programme for its many natural landscapes and relatively few cities. Long stretches of road between the main stops cross steppes, fjords and the foothills of the Andes. Logistics therefore matter as much as the excursions: domestic flights shorten the longest distances, while overland journeys retain the sections where the road itself is part of the experience.

Buenos Aires and Santiago form the 2 city bookends of the route. At the start, Buenos Aires offers tango, architecture and restaurants; at the end, Santiago returns you to a more urban pace after several days among glaciers, steppes and the Strait of Magellan.
